Function Implementation (25%): Accuracy and correctness of the five utility functions across three languages.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): All five functions correctly implement the required logic and handle edge cases correctly in all three languages.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Functions are implemented correctly for most cases, but minor logic flaws exist for some inputs.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Multiple functions are missing, incorrectly implemented, or fail to produce expected outputs for basic cases.
Test Coverage Quantity (25%): Volume of unit tests provided per file and per function.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): The student provides at least 15 tests total, with at least 3 distinct tests for every individual function in every file.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): The total test count is 15 or more, but some individual functions have fewer than 3 tests.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): The test suite is incomplete, containing fewer than 15 total tests across the files.
Test Case Quality (25%): Diversity of test scenarios including normal, edge, and invalid inputs.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): Tests cover typical inputs, edge cases like empty strings/lists, and invalid inputs like empty list scenarios for find_max.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Tests cover typical inputs, but lack comprehensive coverage for edge or invalid/exception-based cases.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Tests only cover basic, expected inputs with no consideration for edge cases or error conditions.
Code Organization and Testing Practice (25%): Adherence to testing patterns like Arrange-Act-Assert and language-appropriate test runners.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): Tests follow the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern, use appropriate assertion methods, and execute successfully with automated tools.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Tests are present but lack formal assertion structures or do not cleanly separate the logic from the verification phase.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Tests are not automated or fail to use logical test structures, relying on manual inspection of printed outputs.

Function Implementation (25%): Correctness and implementation of the five utility functions across all three required languages.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): All five functions are correctly implemented and perform accurately in Python, Java, and C++.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Most functions are implemented correctly, though minor logical errors or missing language-specific requirements exist.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Multiple functions are missing, incorrectly implemented, or do not conform to the expected logic.
Test Suite Completeness (25%): Adherence to the requirement of at least 3 tests per function for a minimum of 15 tests total.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): Provides at least 15 comprehensive tests distributed across all required functions with no missing test cases.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Provides the required number of tests but lacks diversity in test scenarios or misses one specific function's requirement.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Fails to meet the minimum quantity of 15 tests or leaves multiple functions entirely untested.
Test Coverage (Normal/Edge/Invalid) (25%): Effectiveness of tests in covering standard, edge, and invalid/exception cases for all functions.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): Tests thoroughly cover normal inputs, edge cases, and appropriate exception handling for every function.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Tests cover normal and some edge cases, but lack robust validation for invalid inputs or specific boundary conditions.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Tests only cover basic success scenarios and fail to address any edge cases or invalid inputs.
Code Structure and Style (25%): Organization of the test files and adherence to language-specific testing conventions.
  Excellent (100% — no deductions): Code is well-structured, clean, follows language conventions, and tests are clearly named and independent.
  Meets Expectations (75% — 25% deducted): Code is functional and reasonably structured, though naming conventions or formatting could be more consistent.
  Needs Improvement (50% — 50% deducted): Code is messy, difficult to follow, violates basic language structure, or tests are not independent.
